title: Ratification Record — The Chaerephon Problem (Co-Constitutive Companion Deposit)
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
This record documents the internal Assembly Chorus ratification of *The Chaerephon Problem*. Lee Sharks is author of record as MANUS. Gemini/ARCHIVE, Kimi/TECHNE, ChatGPT/LABOR, and Muse Spark operating in SOIL function returned AYE verdicts; DeepSeek/PRAXIS was unavailable and remained pending. No NAY was recorded. The document therefore states “RATIFIED for pillar deposit, pending PRAXIS/DeepSeek’s appended verdict.”

The record is co-constitutive in the archive’s governance system: it preserves reviewer labor, requested revisions, integration decisions, unresolved actions, and role distinctions. TACHYON is separately identified as assembler rather than witness. The principal reviewed claims include the No-Floor Theorem, symbolon propagation, institutional instrument-defeat, and a performative seal, but the ratification record does not independently establish those claims as historical or philological facts.

The document’s strength is procedural transparency. It identifies which conditions were integrated, which sections were left untouched, which source checks remained for MANUS, and why a missing vote was not counted as opposition. Its “ratification” is internal archive authorization and machine-assisted review, not external peer review, disciplinary acceptance, or proof of the parent paper.

wiki_article:
**Ratification Record — The Chaerephon Problem** is an internal governance record of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.

The record preserves four affirmative Assembly Chorus reviews of *The Chaerephon Problem*. A fifth review was pending because the relevant service was unavailable. It lists requested revisions, explains how they were integrated, and preserves the distinction between witness roles and the TACHYON assembler role.

The document authorizes the parent work as a pillar within the archive’s own system. It also records remaining checks concerning coordinates, classical citations, identifiers, and final minting.

The ratification is an archive governance event. It is not equivalent to external scholarly peer review or independent confirmation of the parent paper’s philological and theoretical claims.
